title: Bands heard as a boy on the Mississippi coast
summary: Handy recalls hearing Sam Morgan, Chris Kelly, Punch Miller and the Maple Leaf Band, and the trolley excursions from Biloxi.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I was wondering about some of the bands you heard when you were a kid. When you were very young, before you even started playing. Do you remember any other than your father's band?

I mentioned the few I heard. As a matter of fact, I heard practically all of them because they used to come out there on that coast. Such as Sam Morgan, Chris Kelly, Riddick, Riddick, Riddick, Punch Miller. Uh, a band used to come out there called the Maple Leaf Band. That was with, uh, Freddie Kepert. He used to lead that band. And all those boys used to come out there. I used to hear them. Matter of fact, they used to have what you call a trolley ride from Biloxi to Peskristad. It hooked five or six, uh, trolley cars together. Like an excursion train. And they'd come down there. Oh, they'd have eight or nine hundred of them on there. They'd come down there. They used to have a place there called a profillion. Just the top on it and the floor, no sides. And, uh, summer place, you know. And they'd come down there, dance for four hours. And a trolley car would pull right back up in front of the place. And, uh, everybody would load up on their trolley car. And go on back to Biloxi. Or either they would leave Biloxi some, one time and then go, I mean, leave Peskristad and go to Biloxi. And, uh, my daddy used to play a lot of them. Then he used to get, a lot of time he used to get savvy. It's different bands he used to get.
